Q:2:1:p: Which control is the MOST effective in the hierarchy of control?
Q:2:2:p: Separating forklifts and pedestrians with physical barriers is an example of:
Q:2:2:e: Physically separating people from the hazard is isolation.
Q:2:3:p: Before a spotter guides you with hand signals, you should:
Q:2:3:e: Agree on the signals before starting so there is no confusion.
Q:2:3:o2: Agree on the signals you will both use
Q:2:3:o3: Ask them to stand behind the forklift
Q:2:3:o4: Raise the load so they can see it
Q:2:4:p: Why is operating an LPG forklift in a poorly ventilated area a hazard?
Q:2:4:e: LPG, petrol and diesel engines produce carbon monoxide, which builds up in poorly ventilated areas.
Q:2:4:o4: Carbon monoxide from the exhaust can build up
Q:2:5:p: You need to drive over a steel trench cover. What must you check first?
Q:2:5:e: It must be rated for the combined weight of the forklift and load, and secured.
Q:2:5:o1: That it is rated for the combined weight of the forklift and load
Q:2:5:o3: That it is wider than the forklift
Q:2:5:o4: Nothing — steel is always strong enough
Q:2:6:p: A thunderstorm with lightning moves in while you're working outside. You should:
Q:2:6:e: Stop outdoor work, park the forklift safely and take shelter.
Q:2:6:o1: Speed up to finish the job
Q:2:6:o2: Raise the mast to keep loads dry
Q:2:6:o3: Stop work, park safely and take shelter
Q:2:6:o4: Keep working but stay in the seat
Q:2:7:p: The yard is wet after rain. How should you change the way you drive?
Q:2:7:e: Wet surfaces reduce grip: slow down, brake and turn gently, and allow longer stopping distances.
Q:2:7:o2: Reduce speed and allow longer stopping distances
Q:2:7:o3: Drive faster to get out of the rain
Q:2:8:p: A pedestrian walks into the exclusion zone while you're loading a truck. You:
Q:2:8:e: Stop work immediately until the person has left the zone, then report the breach if required.
Q:2:8:o1: Sound the horn and keep working
Q:2:8:o2: Keep going — they should know better
Q:2:8:o3: Raise the load higher so it's out of the way
Q:2:8:o4: Stop work until they have left the zone
Q:2:9:p: The mast of your forklift touches an overhead powerline. What should you do FIRST?
Q:2:9:e: Step 1 is STAY: stay seated on the forklift and don't touch any metal parts. Getting off could electrocute you.
Q:2:9:o2: Stay on the forklift and don't touch any metal parts
Q:2:9:o3: Climb down using three points of contact
Q:2:9:o4: Push the line away with a piece of timber
Q:2:10:p: A forklift is touching a powerline. How far away should everyone else stay?
Q:2:10:e: Step 2 is WARN: keep everyone at least 8 metres away, and no one touches the forklift.
Q:2:10:o4: It is safe to stand next to it if you don't touch it
Q:2:11:p: Your forklift is touching a powerline and catches fire. How should you get off?
Q:2:11:e: Step 5 is JUMP — only if you must. Jump clear with feet together, never touching the forklift and the ground at the same time, then shuffle with feet together at least 8 m away.
Q:2:11:o1: Jump clear with feet together, then shuffle with feet together at least 8 m away
Q:2:11:o2: Climb down slowly holding the handrail
Q:2:11:o3: Step down and run away as fast as you can
Q:2:11:o4: Stay on the forklift no matter what
Q:2:12:p: What is the correct order of the 5-step powerline contact protocol?
Q:2:12:e: Stay → Warn → Break contact (if safe) → Call for help → Jump clear (only if you must).
Q:2:12:o4: Stay, Warn, Break contact, Call, Jump clear
Q:2:13:e: A hazard is anything that could cause harm — injury, illness or damage. Risk is the chance it will cause harm, and how bad that harm would be.
Q:2:13:o2: The chance that someone will be hurt
Q:2:13:o3: A report you fill in after an incident
Q:2:13:o4: A control such as a barrier
Q:2:14:e: Risk combines likelihood (how likely the hazard is to cause harm) and consequence (how bad the harm would be).
Q:2:14:o3: How likely a hazard is to cause harm, and how bad the harm would be
Q:2:14:o4: The cost of fixing a forklift
Q:2:15:p: Pedestrians often walk through the loading bay where you work. Which statement is correct?
Q:2:15:e: The pedestrians in your work area are the hazard. Being struck by the forklift — likely, and possibly fatal — is the risk.
Q:2:15:o1: The pedestrians are the risk; being hit is the hazard
Q:2:15:o2: The pedestrians are the hazard; the chance of hitting one, and how bad it would be, is the risk
Q:2:15:o3: There is no hazard if pedestrians wear hi-vis
Q:2:15:o4: Hazards and risks mean exactly the same thing
Q:2:16:p: A hazard is likely to happen and could kill someone. How should you rate the risk?
Q:2:16:e: Likely + a serious consequence = high risk. Control it before you start work.
Q:2:16:o2: Medium — it depends on the day
Q:2:16:o3: No risk if you are careful
Q:2:16:o4: High — control it before you start work
Q:3:1:p: When should a pre-start check be carried out?
Q:3:1:e: Pre-start checks are done before every shift, before the forklift is used.
Q:3:2:p: A side shifter has been fitted to the forklift. What must you check on the data plate?
Q:3:2:e: The data plate must match the attachment fitted, because attachments change capacity.
Q:3:2:o1: That it shows the purchase date
Q:3:2:o2: That it is the same colour as the forklift
Q:3:2:o3: That it is correct for the attachment fitted
Q:3:3:p: During the walk-around you see flaking paint around a weld on the mast. This could indicate:
Q:3:3:e: Paint separation around welds can be a sign of a crack or stressed weld underneath. Record and report it.
Q:3:3:o1: A crack or stressed weld underneath
Q:3:3:o3: Normal wear that can be ignored
Q:3:4:p: How should you get on and off a forklift?
Q:3:4:e: Use the steps and handholds with three points of contact. Never jump.
Q:3:4:o2: Use the steering wheel to swing off
Q:3:4:o4: Use the steps and handholds with three points of contact
Q:3:5:p: During operational checks, the hydraulic functions should be:
Q:3:5:e: Run lift, tilt and side shift through their full range and check they move smoothly.
Q:3:5:o1: Tested only if the load is heavy
Q:3:5:o2: Run through their full range to check smooth operation
Q:3:5:o4: Tested with a full load at maximum height
Q:3:6:p: What is the correct order for lock out / tag out?
Q:3:6:e: Stop and park safely, isolate the power, tag it out of service, then report and record the fault.
Q:3:6:o1: Stop, isolate the power, tag it, report it
Q:3:6:o2: Report it, then keep using it until it's collected
Q:3:6:o3: Tag it, keep the engine running, report it
Q:3:6:o4: Remove the tag, then report it
Q:3:7:p: Your forklift begins to tip over sideways. What should you do?
Q:3:7:e: Never jump. Stay in the seat with the belt on, hold the wheel, brace your feet and lean away from the fall.
Q:3:7:o1: Jump clear on the low side
Q:3:7:o2: Jump clear on the high side
Q:3:7:o3: Stay seated with the seatbelt on, hold the wheel, brace and lean away from the fall
Q:3:7:o4: Raise the mast to rebalance it
Q:3:8:p: Your LPG forklift starts to stutter and lose power. The most likely cause is:
Q:3:8:e: A stuttering LPG engine usually means the cylinder is running empty. Park safely and change it following procedure.
Q:3:8:o2: The gas cylinder is running empty
Q:4:1:p: The stability triangle of a counterbalance forklift is formed by:
Q:4:1:e: The two front wheels and the rear axle pivot point form the stability triangle.
Q:4:1:o2: The two front wheels and the rear axle pivot point
Q:4:1:o3: The mast and the two front wheels
Q:4:2:p: What does the rated capacity on a forklift's data plate tell you?
Q:4:2:e: The rated capacity is the maximum weight the forklift can safely lift. Never lift more than it.
Q:4:2:o3: The maximum weight it can safely lift
Q:4:2:o4: How high the mast can reach
Q:4:3:p: A pallet has 40 cartons weighing 20 kg each. The pallet weighs 20 kg. What is the total weight?
Q:4:3:e: 40 × 20 = 800 kg, plus the 20 kg pallet = 820 kg.
Q:4:4:p: Which document from a transport company may show the weight of a load?
Q:4:4:e: Consignment notes and running sheets often list the weight of each item.
Q:4:5:p: You can't find the weight of a load anywhere. What should you do?
Q:4:5:e: Never guess. Don't lift until the weight is confirmed — ask your supervisor or weigh it.
